result.title: The Flip Test: Video World Models Fail to Learn the World State
result.summary: Video world models promise to predict the future of a scene from its present. Do current models keep this promise? We probe this question counterfactually. When a small change to the present flips the future, such as a box resting a few millimeters before or past a table edge, a model that tracks the state of the world must flip its prediction too. We build FlipTest, a three-level hierarchy of increasingly strict tests over 1,680 initial frames from 10 simulated and 15 real-world tasks. At the base, visual minimal pairs, two nearly identical frames whose true futures differ, test whether predictions change across the boundary; matched controls go further and test whether they change only where the future does; and dense sweeps, the strictest level, locate exactly where they change. All 11 video world models we evaluate fall short. The best averages 18.3% pair accuracy over real and simulated scenes, below the 25% of random guessing. Models flip as often on steps that leave the future unchanged as on steps that change it, and their response stays flat across the sweeps. On the same frames, a vision-language model is selective and traces a near S-shaped curve near the boundary, and a coding agent that measures the image comes close to the true boundary. This implies that the deciding information is in the frame, and video models just miss it. We therefore urge the community to rethink world modeling as pure video prediction. Next-frame prediction must do more than draw plausible pixels; it must also identify the causal states that control future dynamics.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 FlipTest：以视觉最小对、匹配对照和密集扫描三层递进的反事实测试，在 1,680 帧、25 个仿真与真实任务上检验 11 个视频世界模型能否在「箱子位于桌沿前/后几毫米」这类边界处翻转未来预测，结果显示所有模型均失败；同帧上的 VLM 与测量图像的编码代理则能定位边界。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作直接诊断预测式模型是否把控制未来动力学的因果状态编码进内部表示，而非只生成合理像素；其最小对／密集扫描探针可供核查 LVR 中视觉证据与关键状态是否真正进入 latent 并影响输出，也提示「用反事实边界检验状态敏感性」这一评价思路。
